# openobserve_composite_alert (Data Source)

Reads an existing composite alert, looked up either by `alert_id` or by `name`.

Alongside the configuration, this reports what the composite currently sees: each child's severity, whether that child's state has gone stale, and how it evaluated. That is the fastest way to answer why a composite is or is not firing without opening the UI.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "openobserve_composite_alert" "bad_deploy" {
  name = "checkout-bad-deploy"
}

# Why is it firing, or why is it not? `children` carries the state the
# composite actually read, which is the fastest way to answer that.
output "children_currently_true" {
  value = [
    for child in data.openobserve_composite_alert.bad_deploy.children :
    child.name if child.truth
  ]
}

# A stale child is not contributing its last value; it is contributing whatever
# stale_child_policy says. That distinction is usually the answer to "why did
# this not fire".
output "stale_children" {
  value = [
    for child in data.openobserve_composite_alert.bad_deploy.children :
    child.name if child.stale
  ]
}

# Null until the composite has been evaluated once, which is not the same as
# having evaluated to false.
output "last_result" {
  value = try(data.openobserve_composite_alert.bad_deploy.evaluation.result, null)
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `alert_id` (String) Composite alert identifier. Supply this or `name`.
- `folder_id` (String) Restrict a name lookup to one folder. All folders are searched when omitted.
- `name` (String) Composite alert name. Supply this or `alert_id`.
- `org_id` (String) Organization identifier. Defaults to the provider's `org_id`.

### Read-Only

- `children` (Attributes List) The children the expression resolves to, in expression order, each with the state the composite read from it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--children))
- `description` (String) What the composite watches for.
- `destinations` (Set of String) Destinations notified when the composite fires.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the composite is evaluated.
- `evaluation` (Attributes) The composite's own most recent verdict. Null when it has never been evaluated, which is a different thing from having evaluated to false. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--evaluation))
- `expression` (String) The stored boolean expression, in the fully parenthesized form the server canonicalizes to.
- `id` (String) Data source ID in the format `{org_id}/{alert_id}`.
- `priority` (Number) Configured priority, 1 (most urgent) to 5.
- `scheduler_job_present` (Boolean) Whether a scheduler job currently backs this composite.
- `silence` (Number) Minutes the composite stays quiet after firing.
- `stale_child_policy` (String) What a stale child contributes to the expression.
- `tags` (Set of String) Selection tags on the composite.
- `warning_counts_as_firing` (Boolean) Whether a child at warning severity counts as true.

<a id="nestedatt--children"></a>
### Nested Schema for `children`

Read-Only:

- `accessible` (Boolean) Whether the caller may read this child. When false every other attribute here is null, and the composite still evaluates it.
- `alert_id` (String) Child alert identifier.
- `alert_type` (String) Child kind: `scheduled`, `slo`, or `composite`.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the child is evaluated.
- `folder_id` (String) Folder holding the child.
- `level` (String) Severity of the child's last classification: `ok`, `warning`, or `critical`.
- `level_at` (Number) When `level` was recorded, in microseconds.
- `name` (String) Child alert name.
- `stale` (Boolean) Whether the child's state is older than three times its own cadence. A stale child contributes whatever `stale_child_policy` dictates rather than its last value.
- `truth` (Boolean) What this child contributed to the expression on the last evaluation.


<a id="nestedatt--evaluation"></a>
### Nested Schema for `evaluation`

Read-Only:

- `evaluated_at` (Number) When the result was recorded, in microseconds.
- `level` (String) Severity of the result.
- `result` (Boolean) Whether the expression evaluated true.
